summary.one_liner: Mutahunter is an open-source, language-agnostic mutation testing tool that uses LLMs to generate code mutants and report how many your test suite catches.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a CLI called "mutahunter run" that takes a test command, a model name, a source file path, and a test file path. It uses an LLM (the example uses gpt-4o-mini, with an OpenAI API key) to create mutants of the source file, runs the test command against each mutant, and labels each as killed or survived. It also reports compile-error and timeout mutants separately. At the end it prints an overall mutation coverage percentage, mutant counts, and the total LLM cost in USD. The example output shows a Java Maven project, and the README says there are further examples for other languages in an examples directory.
use_cases: measure how well unit tests catch bugs
run mutation testing on Java Maven projects
find weak spots in a test suite
estimate LLM cost of mutation testing runs
how_to_run: pip install (package installed via GitHub; Python 3.11+ required)
notable: Language-agnostic: the test command is supplied by the user, so any test runner can be used
LLM-generated mutants rather than rule-based operators
Reports mutation coverage, killed/survived counts, and total LLM cost per run
Includes a Java example in the examples directory
caveats: Requires an OpenAI API key and incurs LLM usage costs
The README's install command is missing its package reference, so the exact install step is unclear from the text
The README does not describe platform support beyond the examples shown
keywords: check how good my tests are
